title: Amalfi, slowly
world_prompt: The Amalfi Coast in Italy on a bright summer morning. Pastel houses stacked up a steep cliff above a turquoise bay, lemon trees on terraces, small wooden boats in the harbour, a winding coastal road. Cinematic travel film, warm golden light, slow graceful camera.

beats.scene: A slow, wide establishing shot of the pastel town on the cliff above the turquoise bay in morning light.

beats.line: Where mornings begin with lemons, and the smell of the sea.
beats.scene: The camera drifts gently along a terrace of lemon trees, sunlight through the leaves, the sea glittering below.

beats.line: Where the road hugs the cliff, and every turn is a postcard.
beats.scene: The camera follows the narrow coastal road as it curves around the cliff, the bay opening up below.

beats.line: Seven days of boat trips, long lunches, and evenings that never hurry.
beats.scene: A small wooden boat glides across the calm turquoise water toward the harbour.

beats.line: Meridian. Amalfi, slowly. Curious about anything? Just ask.
beats.scene: The camera rises slowly over the harbour and the whole town in warm golden light.

facts.package: Seven nights on the Amalfi Coast, staying in Positano, in a sea-view room at a small family-run hotel.
facts.price: From 2,450 US dollars per person, including flights from New York, hotel, breakfast, and a private boat day.
facts.dates: Departures every Saturday from May to October. June and September are the sweet spot: warm sea, fewer crowds.
facts.getting_there: Fly into Naples, then a ninety-minute private transfer along the coast road, included.
facts.included: Flights, seven nights' hotel, breakfast, airport transfers, a private boat day to Capri, and a lemon-grove cooking class in Ravello.
facts.not_included: Lunches and dinners, except the cooking class. Travel insurance.
facts.beach: The hotel is a four-minute walk down the steps to Spiaggia Grande, Positano's main beach.
facts.night: Evenings are slow: dinner on a terrace, the harbour lit up, a limoncello on the waterfront.
facts.weather: Summer is 27 to 31 degrees Celsius and sunny. Spring and autumn are mild, around 20 to 24.
facts.food: Fresh seafood, lemon everything, handmade pasta, and the cooking class in Ravello.
facts.kids: Families welcome. Positano has a lot of stairs, so a light stroller or a carrier works best.
facts.booking: Book at meridian dot travel slash amalfi. Free cancellation up to thirty days before departure.
facts.brand: Meridian is a small-group and independent travel company. This trip is independent: your own pace, with a local host on call.
